subject: Replica expiry path & legal-hold interaction — evidence and timelines
messages:
From: compliance@greenbank.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on replica expiry during legal hold

Hi Sean,

We are preparing for a third-party audit and need clarification on how Redwood handles backup replica expiry when a legal hold is placed on a customer dataset. Specific asks: 

- If a dataset has a 90-day backup TTL and a legal hold is applied on day 45, do existing replicas get extended automatically or do they expire on the original schedule?
- What evidence (logs, audit trail) can you provide showing the hold was honored and that no replicas were removed while the hold was active?
- If a hold is applied to a subset of keys (e.g., accounts in EU region), how is cross-region replica replication handled during the hold?

We would like a short written statement and an exportable evidence package for the audit ideally by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Greenbank Compliance
compliance@greenbank.com

---
Attachment: request_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet list of datasets)
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: compliance@greenbank.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on replica expiry during legal hold

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Security) and Naomi (Infra) to confirm exact behavior and the evidence package. Quick answers while they assemble the export: 

- Holds prevent garbage collection of snapshots/replicas tagged by the hold id; they are not auto-deleted while the hold is active.
- We can produce an audit bundle: hold creation event, affected object ids, GC skip logs, and a snapshot manifest.
- Cross-region replication: holds are applied at the dataset object level; replication continues but GC is inhibited on all replicas that carry the hold tag.

Monica/Naomi — could you confirm timing guarantees (e.g., when a replica would have been scheduled for expiry and the specific logs we can export), and confirm a timeline for the evidence package? Sara — I’ll follow up with a formal note and the bundle by 2026-01-21 EOD.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, compliance@greenbank.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on replica expiry during legal hold

Hi all,

Confirming the behavioral details and the evidence we can provide. High-level: 

- Hold semantics: when a legal hold is attached (internal tag: hold_<id>), the GC worker checks for that tag and skips expiration for any snapshot/replica carrying it. That prevents deletion even if TTL has passed.

- Proof artifacts we will produce: 
  * hold_creation_event.json (timestamp, user id, hold id)
  * snapshot_manifest_<date>.csv (list of snapshot ids + regions + original expiry)
  * gc_skip_logs_<range>.log (entries where GC found hold tag and skipped deletion)
  * replication_audit.log (replication events for affected snapshot ids)

- Timing note: If a replica was scheduled for deletion and GC already started a compaction pass before hold was applied, we may have a narrow race window (~minutes). We have compensating checks: object tombstone state is reversible if compaction did not remove underlying blocks. We will flag any such items in the evidence bundle.

I attached a simple retention_matrix_v2.pdf that maps TTL classes to expected GC windows and the tag behaviors. Naomi — can you add the exact command/history to extract the gc_skip_logs and point me to the retention export?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.pdf
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, compliance@greenbank.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on replica expiry during legal hold

Hi — adding infra specifics and an exported snippet below. TL;DR: hold tag prevents GC across replicas and regions; we can produce a timebound evidence bundle.

Export notes (commands we ran):
- export_snapshot_manifest --dataset gb-prod-accounts --since 2025-12-01 --format csv 
  produced snapshot_manifest_20260119.csv (included in bundle).
- query_gc_logs --start 2026-01-01T00:00Z --end 2026-01-19T23:59Z --filter hold_tag:hold_GB-2026-001 
  produced gc_skip_logs_20260101-19.log (sample below).

Sample from gc_skip_logs_20260101-19.log:
[2026-01-15T09:41:23Z] GC_WORKER shard-37: snapshot s-8f3a hold_tag=hold_GB-2026-001 — SKIP_EXPUNGE
[2026-01-15T09:41:23Z] GC_WORKER shard-37: replica r-24b1 region=us-west-2 hold_tag=hold_GB-2026-001 — SKIP_EXPUNGE

Replica TTL semantics: replica metadata has two fields: created_at and scheduled_expire_at. When a hold is applied we write hold_meta{hold_id, applied_at} and reconcile scheduled_expire_at to null for GC decisions. We do not rewrite the created_at; scheduled_expire_at is treated as overridden while the hold exists.

Cross-region nuance: for cross-region replicated objects, the hold meta is replicated asynchronously. For short windows between hold application and replication propagation (~seconds to a minute) a remote GC worker could see the original scheduled_expire_at. We minimize this with an immediate hold-broadcast message; we will highlight any object ids that fell into that window in the bundle.

Bundle ETA: 2026-01-21 by 17:00 PST. Included files: snapshot_manifest_20260119.csv, gc_skip_logs_20260101-19.log, replication_audit_20260119.log, metadata_export_hold_GB-2026-001.json. Also creating a one-page attestation on Redwood letterhead.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: compliance@greenbank.com, audit@datacust.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on replica expiry during legal hold

Sara / DataCust auditors — attached is the evidence bundle and our short attestation. Key points: 

- Holds inhibit GC on all replicas that surface the hold tag; scheduled expirations are treated as overridden while the hold is active.
- We have identified zero replicas that were irreversibly expunged between hold application and broadcast. Any object in the narrow propagation window where the remote region GC may have seen the original TTL is flagged in the manifest (column: hold_race_flag).
- Included artifacts: retention_matrix_v2.pdf, snapshot_manifest_20260119.csv, gc_skip_logs_20260101-19.log, replication_audit_20260119.log, metadata_export_hold_GB-2026-001.json, attestation_redwood_20260121.pdf

Next steps: please confirm whether you need the raw block-level manifests (larger export) or if the provided bundle satisfies the audit. If you need additional evidence, we can schedule a short call to walk the bundle on Friday.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
